newsitem.title: GERMANY: German cash cocoa market lacks incentive.
newsitem.headline: German cash cocoa market lacks incentive.

text.p: Physical cocoa markets in Germany are dormant amid steadier conditions in futures and the strength of sterling, traders said on Thursday.
"Large international operators have a high level of coverage for 15-18 months," one said.
"The medium-sized industry in Europe is interested in levels below 1,000 stg in London and below $1,450 in New York, which both look unobtainable at the moment."
At 1500 GMT, London September was unchanged at 1,028 stg a tonne.
Traders expected futures to remain range-bound and low in volume in the medium term with fundamentals unchanged.
One said trader ED&F Man's cut in its world 1996/97 supply deficit forecast was neutral because a small deficit at this stage in the season was not unusual.
There was no apparent shortage of cocoa and estimates for the season may well turn into a surplus later on.
Man earlier pegged the 1996/97 deficit at 125,000-150,000 tonnes from the 170,000-230,000 estimated in January.
West African beans were quoted up on the week at 2.77 marks per kilo cif for the second quarter (2.71 last week), 2.79 for the third quarter (2.75) and 2.79 (2.72) for the fourth quarter.
The cocoa butter ratio was at 2.41 spot (2.40), at 2.44 for the third (2.45) and at 2.51 (2.52) for the fourth quarter.
Implied mark prices liquid ex-works were higher at 6.88 (6.70), 7.01 (6.84) and 7.08 (6.94) respectively.
